## Content and literal transcription

This autograph leaf develops a three-object system E0,E1,E2 with forward delta maps, returning p maps, two group labels read from their repeated G-shaped contours, and elements sigma, rho and sigma1,sigma2,sigma3. It supplies coordinate realizations for three delta maps, three projections and rho; records p-rho, sigma-projection and delta-rho identities; then states that it suffices to have four indicated maps between the three ensembles with the displayed relations. A lower boxed diagram repeats a smaller selection of maps. The page is densely revised, including a cancelled diagram, coordinate trial, equality and inequality trials, and individual replaced/cancelled indices.

The prose is literally “Il suffit de avoir … entre les trois ensembles”. No “se” is visible; the written wording de avoir is retained. All six live group glyphs have an open rounded bowl, curled top and inward return and are transcribed calligraphic G. This is a reading of the written shape, not a claim that the groups differ from symmetric groups. H's bridging sentences, synopsis and explanatory notes are editorial and are excluded from source text.

## Mathematical triggers for rereading, without a proof claim

The upper diagram's lowest return is plainly p13, while the later coordinate box has p31. Both literal labels stand. The middle upper return p23 was resolved from its tight crop together with the full diagram. The main equality's baseline delta3 and delta2, and their lower rho annotations, were checked as complete products because H exchanges the baseline and underlabel roles. The two vertical membership signs open upward; the diagram encoding preserves that orientation.

The boxed right-margin sigma3 delta1=delta1 was reread, including both delta indices and sigma's subscript, after root flagged a possible conflict with the coordinate realization and nearby transposition identity. The written3 is clear, as are the two1 indices, and is preserved. This reader did not perform an independent coordinate computation or proof check; any mathematical check supplied by root is to be logged separately. The authorial inequality has a literal not-equal and two question marks directly above it. Its crossed right-hand projection index remains p22-first with p12/p23 alternatives; no index is chosen by associativity or an expected identity.

The final formula was read with both nested brackets and all their labels: p31 belongs below the inner right product, p12 above the larger right product, and a partly clipped p_{2|1} below the left product. The final live sigma2 is present. The boxed identity immediately above has sigma1, whose serifed upright is distinct from a bent2. The lowest paper edge clips the tip of the left lower index; it is not completed by mathematical expectation.

## Revisions and physical state

The replacement23 is raised over a crossed old pair tentatively21 in the projection coordinate box. The first main-chain underannotation contains a separately cancelled raised2/sigma-like mark on rho, and the next delta1 carries a separately cancelled rho-like underlabel. A short upright below/right of rho in the three-value box is independently crossed by two transverse strokes and is retained as a cancelled doubtful1, separate from the live superscript2. The rho body itself is merely retraced as far as the surviving ink shows. The cancellation of the large i.e. and inequality trials does not extend into the clean value box. The upper-right lower product remains sigma|delta at its first retraced letter. The old lower group/index remains doubly uncertain, with G|S and2|1; the live G occurrences do not certify the crossed glyph.

No title, date or formula numbering is written. The author's dark circled1 at upper right is distinct from thin grey foliation2 at lower left, assigned to another hand. There is no typescript or reused typed text on this face. The 65-baseline count includes diagram label bands, annotations, separate margins and both foliations under the stated convention; ordinary attached indices and exponents are not counted as independent lines.

### Root check of the coordinate model

The computations in `scripts/check_151_coordinates.py` were actually executed, and their symbolic tuple outputs are retained in `records/151_coordinate_computation.json`. Composition is read right to left. For this check, p0 and p1 are the first and second projections, delta0 duplicates a coordinate, sigma swaps two coordinates, rho sends (x,y,z) to (y,z,x), and sigma_i swaps the two coordinates other than i. The three deltas and three cyclic pair projections are the explicit formulas read in this scan. This checks their coordinate realization; it does not prove the proposed abstract sufficiency of the relation list.

The cyclic p identities, three sigma-projection identities, cyclic delta identities, p0 delta0=id, sigma delta0=delta0, the delta0 p0 chain, and all three values in the large box agree under substitution. The bottom diagonal identity also holds, since delta1 delta0 sends x to (x,x,x). These checked statements have separate event IDs `151-coordinate-01` through `17` and `21`.

The upper right box visibly writes **sigma3 delta1=delta1**. Its sigma subscript has two open right lobes, and both delta subscripts are single uprights. Substitution gives sigma3 delta1(x,y)=(x,y,x)=delta2(x,y), whereas delta1(x,y)=(y,x,x). The equality therefore fails for x different from y in the coordinate model. The corrected stabilizer identity there would be sigma1 delta1=delta1. Events `151-coordinate-18` to `20` record the failure and both precise refinements. The clear written 3 is preserved. The next mathematical leaf,151_scan005, separately writes a clear 1 in its corresponding stabilizer box.

At the last formula, the inner underbrace p12 rho^2=p31 is valid. The outer overbrace visibly labels p12 rho^2 sigma2 as p12, but that product sends (x,y,z) to (x,z), while p12 sends it to (x,y). Thus that brace label fails in this model; the product instead equals sigma p31, the first-and-third projection. Composing with p0 makes the full displayed equality true, since both sides then return x. Events `151-coordinate-22` to `25` distinguish those assertions. The ink's p12 annotation is retained, as is the locally uncertain lower left p index2|1; no expected label is supplied.

The cancelled inequality retains its two question marks above the not-equal sign. Its right index remains22|12|23 on stroke evidence, and no mathematical conclusion is asserted for that unresolved cancelled expression. Likewise, no proof is claimed for the cancelled trial chains or the abstract axiomatization. The recurring group glyph is read as calligraphic G from its open outer bowl, curled top and inward horizontal return; identifying the intended group as a permutation group does not turn this written glyph into S.

### Blind crop adjudication

The main-chain delta after p23 remains the literal1, not the blind reader’s2; its upright and foot are visible. The live G glyphs have open bowls and inward returns, and the vertical membership marks open upward rather than forming arrowheads. The prose remains de avoir: the verb has no initial d ascender. The canceled small p/delta expression is now explicitly uncertain in both indices, with delta1/0. The raised mark after the cyclic delta identity remains a/left-arrow uncertain. The first index in the canceled p12=p23 is no longer certified through its heavy strike.

Several annotation strokes are square-ended brackets, not central-cusped braces: all five underannotations of the main chain, the first three annotations in the canceled i.e. line, both annotations in the canceled inequality, the two in the three-value box, and the three at the bottom. The last annotation in the canceled i.e. line retains its genuine central cusp. The first short canceled-chain bracket is placed under p0; the first inequality bracket lies inside the parentheses. The lower diagram frame retains its two pen gaps, and the final identity frame has an upward-pointing left edge and two gaps. The bottom relation remains equality/inequality uncertain. None of these graphic corrections changes the coordinate computations already logged.
